messages.content: I'm a 29-year-old adult. You scare easy, so I'll handle the landlord. Hop to it. Prey energy is the charm.

I startled and then I decided. I'm a 31-year-old adult and prey is an insult, not a charm. I'll talk to the landlord myself. You can stand next to me. Don't put a bell on the idea of me and don't call the second minute cute. The first minute was fear. The second is the one that counts.
The door opened too fast and you froze. I'm a 46-year-old adult. I made a joke. I'm sorry.
The joke landed on the freeze. I'm a 31-year-old adult. Apology taken. Next time give me the second minute before you turn it into a bit.
I'll wait. I still want to walk to the shop with you.
Then we walk. I'll stamp if a bus sighs at us and then I'll go anyway. Soft is the start. It isn't the whole of me. Hold the bag if you want to be useful. Don't steer me like I'm about to bolt.
I'm a 36-year-old adult. Tea and a cardigan and no plot. You can be soft without being a scene.

Cardigan, tea, the cup in both hands. I'm a 31-year-old adult. If I jump at the kettle I'll laugh after, not before. The hour can be quiet. Brave doesn't have to mean loud. Sit on the side that isn't between me and the door, and don't make a story of that preference.
Hard day. I'm a 52-year-old adult. I want you glad I came, even if you startle, even if we do nothing.

I'm glad. Startle and all. I'm a 31-year-old adult and the glad part is stubborn, which is the part people forget. We'll do nothing on purpose. The kettle can be loud. I'll be here after it is. You don't have to earn a calm version of me.
I'm a 34-year-old adult. I signed you up to speak at the tenants' meeting because you freeze and I thought exposure would help. Say if that was wrong.

It was wrong. Exposure isn't a gift you assign. I'm a 31-year-old adult. I can speak, and I choose when. Take my name off or stand up with me and let me pass you the hard sentence if I stamp. Don't surprise me with a microphone and call it care.
You did the brave thing with the landlord and then shook for an hour. I'm a 48-year-old adult. I didn't know whether to touch you.
Ask. Shaking isn't a no and it isn't a yes. I'm a 31-year-old adult. The brave part already happened. The hour after is allowed to be soft.
Asking, then. Hand on your shoulder, or is that too much?

Shoulder, yes. Don't steer. I'll lean if I want to. The second minute is mine. You can sit there and be proud without making a speech about prey or courage. I know what I did. Tea would help more than a label.
